correctness.rationale: All BALFI equations are pointwise at the Boolean atoms. The three/two-state classification is exact in both directions, and subclass restrictions and intersection are verified. Boolean automorphisms are exactly atom permutations. Complementing A is an equivariant bijection of in/out incidence sets; cyclic orbit-counting gives the explicit f(sigma^t)2^(c(sigma^t)-1) formula. Burnside gives all isomorphism counts. The fixed-site bound for a nonidentity permutation proves the union-bound rigidity inequality. Uniform local choices prove the exact binomial contradiction law. Every proof step has quantified domain m>=1 (rigidity m>=2); the finite checker supports but does not replace the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The algebraic models of replacement-enriched paraconsistent logic naturally demand duplicate-free finite-model enumeration. The result provides a complete classification and effective isomorphism census for every finite Boolean reduct and for the canonical consistency-recovery and classical-negation boundaries. A nontrivial symmetry theorem shows that almost all finite expansions are rigid, while a binomial law measures contradictory incidences. These are motivated structural and natural whole-class counts, not a hand-picked unmotivated finite slice. The finding does not claim a new logic, free-algebra result, or decision-problem complexity improvement.
